x: We scored a win in the Shot Putt, our Field Event Captain, Bill Sutton, doing 33ft. 10½in., which was too good for the opposition. Thus with three events to go the score was: Belgrave 27, Old Tiffinians 27, but as two of these were the High and Long Jump and, moreover, we had to field Frank Webb in…
Worrad and Bill Sutton were 2nd and 3rd, with 37ft. and 34ft. 9in. respectively.

We are greatly indebted to Bill Sutton, whose details of placings during the race were most helpful. The conditions were excellent for running and the afternoon was warm, bright and sunny, and we, the spectators, had a very good time, with a pleasant coach journey through a beautiful part of Surrey…

A band was engaged and Bill Sutton operated a radio amplifier. Even this did not render Bill free from the sudden (but well-calculated) embraces of one of the ladies, who, after careful manœuvering, caught him unawares.

Fred White, who was making his last appearance for the Club owing to his being called for the R.A.F., finished 2nd. The field events men—Syd Jones and Bill Sutton—gained full points in most of the field events. Charlie Jones also scored in these events.

Bill Sutton was fairly consistent at about his usual distance with the Weight. He still does not seem to be able to reach that 40 feet which might be expected of him.

Bill Sutton also did well in taking second place in the Discus and third in the Weight. The Javelin was won by the ever-green George Pownell, who is still showing the youngsters how to throw a javelin correctly.
Bill Sutton was second in the Weight and also gained third place in the Discus, but Bill seems to miss the support of Syd Jones, our other " strong " man, who is in the Services.
We were very glad to welcome Syd Jones in the Weight, and he won with a fine put of 38ft. 11in. Bill Sutton took second place, with D.
The past season, in spite of a further reduction in active members, has been very successful. Ron Jeal, Charlie Melchoir, George Powell, Bill Sutton, a promising new member, L.
Is Ernie Duffett now the complete " cop "? Do Bill Sutton and Syd Jones still find time to toss the 16 lbs. shot about?
Bill Sutton spent Christmas Day at Catterick, and says he " did not do too bad." Sid Jones, our weight slinger, has gone out East, and more news is awaited.
Patience, Bill Sutton and Ben May, to all of whom we offer our congratulations.—What a team for 1962! We are also pleased to hear that Ron Jeal has become the father of a daughter.—Congrats.
Bill Sutton is now a Lance/Corporal. Has attended several Schools of Instruction, some quite close home, but has failed to find time to contact " Belgravia." Shame Bill!
Pat Ridge, our Irish Guardsman, won both the Weight Put and Discus Throw, and what a trio he, Syd Jones and Bill Sutton would make. We were without Melchior in the Javelin, but B.
In particular we have missed Bill Sutton, one of our most popular and valued exponents. Ron Jeal also has not been able to turn out until the last few matches.

Bill Sutton is also somewhere out in the M.E., and enjoying himself with funny crawly things that wear heavy boots at night. Cyril Pateman, out in Ceylon, is pleased to hear that the Club is carrying on so well, and looking to the day when he may once again join in a Club cross-country race.

Bill Sutton is finding Italy to his liking and has found a good billet with good food (nice work!). Spent a night in the mountains and enjoyed a fall of snow.

In a later letter he reports that he is over the Seine—and then he turns up at the Hall, fit and well. Bill Sutton is now in Corsica in heavily wooded mountainous country with lots of fruit. Is near the sea and has been doing some swimming.

Bill Sutton denies the rumour that he had gained the Military Medal; in fact, he's far behind the lines! He is still in Corsica, and recommends it as ideal walking and climbing country.
Bill Sutton was seen at the Hall recently. Jim Heathfield, another one at Hamburg, previously at Bruges.
Len Rollins has also been promoted to Lt.-Commander, and has been in command of a camp of 700 at Ceylon. Bill Sutton is now a Corporal.

We welcome the return of Sid Jones and Bill Sutton from the Forces and genial Jerry Thompson, after suffering from sugar diabetes, has been one of the features of the Section's activities during the past summer.

Charlie Jones was second in the Long Jump and our "heavy" brigade of Syd Jones and Bill Sutton gained useful points in the Weight Putt. Alan Dunn beat Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw in finishing second to Dalyrymple of L.A.C.

Syd Jones and Bill Sutton were first and second in the Weight, and Syd and Alan Dunn also gained major points in the Discus. Dick Negus was off form in the jumping events and is maybe feeling the effects of a very full season.
The Field Event handicaps were well supported and Bill Sutton and Syd Jones were among the prize-winners, and it was pleasing to see Laurie Jackson gaining a first award.
McKenzie was second for us in the High Jump, thus showing his versatility, Charlie Melchior won the Javelin, and Bill Sutton had a couple of second places in the Weight and Discus.

Bill Sutton was second to Dave Grigg in the Discus Throw, and then Ted Read won the 220 yards and the home team also won the medley relay. In fact the only success registered by our visitors was in the Ladies' Weight Putt, but nevertheless, they showed themselves very good sports, and returned home…

Bill Sutton, our second string, stepped into the breach after Sid's injury and showed a welcome return to his pre-war form with the Shot. He won the Club Championship with an effort of 36 feet 5¼ inches and beat 37 feet once or twice.

Jock Mackenzie in the Discus should again show improvement and will be backed up by Sid Jones and Bill Sutton. Sid and Bill will be our Shot Putters, but Jock Mackenzie and Les Christmas have possibilities if they only get down to training.

In the field events, Bergvalds won the Discus; Bill Sutton was second in the Shot, and George Powell second in the Javelin Throw. The final scores were: L.A.C. and Dorking, 56 points each; Belgrave, 48.
Bill Sutton, Jock Mackenzie and Ans Bergvalds will be available for the Shot and Discus backed up by Doug. Childs, Terry Bateman, Len Higgins, Doug.
Bill Sutton gained third place in the Weight and we did not have any long-jumpers present. The final score in the Senior match was Mitcham A.C. 37; Herne Hill H. 35; Belgrave H. 15.

Bergvalds, our Latvian member, won the Discus and was second in the Shot Putt, with Bill Sutton in third place. Total points in the senior match were:—Cambridge H. 37½; Belgrave H. 34½; Blackheath H. 31.
Ches Walker won the 440 yards, with Odde in second place, and Jack Brown won the 880, with Archie Bedford fourth. Bill Sutton, D.
Allen won the Weight, with Bill Sutton second and Maclean and Holtum " obliged " in the High Jump in order to score points for third and fourth places.
We hope Bergvalds will get better support and look to Arthur Allen and Dennis Childs for this, as we cannot expect Bill Sutton to go on for ever.
John Bromley won the 2 miles run with Archie Bedford in 2nd place, and in the field events we had Luxon, Childs and Bill Sutton picking up a few points here and there.
Luxon in a similar position in the Long Jump event. Bill Sutton was third in the Weight and the final match points were—Herne Hill H., 60; Belgrave H., 38; Cambridge H., 23.
